summary.text: A 48-year-old woman with a history of two cesarean deliveries underwent robotic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy for multiple uterine fibroids associated with abnormal uterine bleeding. To facilitate dissection of the vesicouterine plane, intravesical ICG (25 mg diluted in 200 mL of normal saline and sterile water) was administered through a temporarily clamped Foley catheter.

Initial dissection of the vesicouterine space showed opened peritoneum and anterior fibrotic bands from prior cesarean delivery. After intravesical ICG instillation, Firefly near-infrared imaging showed inconsistent, patchy and incomplete bladder wall fluorescence, limited to non-scarred areas, with non-fluorescent scarred regions superiorly. The surgery was completed robotically without complications and without injury to the bladder or ureters.

summary.text: A 43-year-old woman with deep infiltrating endometriosis, described as advanced endometriosis with significant adhesions, underwent robotic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Preoperative MRI revealed extensive deep pelvic endometrial implants and the right ureter in close proximity to the posterior uterine wall.

Cystoscopic retrograde instillation of ICG, 12.5 mg diluted in 5 mL normal saline, was performed into each ureter. Robotic exposure showed an obliterated posterior compartment with distorted planes. After deep posterior endometriosis excision, landmarks were restored, and Firefly imaging showed continuous ureteral fluorescence without interruption or leakage.

At the end of surgery, after hysterectomy and endometriosis excision, Firefly imaging showed clear visualization of the ureteral course with intact anatomy, preserved vascularity and no evidence of injury. Retrograde ICG gave uniform and strong ureteral fluorescence, and the procedure was completed without complications.

summary.text: A 29-year-old patient with stage 3 endometriosis, described as advanced endometriosis with significant adhesions, underwent robotic endometriosis excision. Preoperative MRI showed a multiloculated cystic lesion in the right adnexa consistent with a tubo-ovarian endometrioma, a unilocular left ovarian endometrioma, and kissing ovaries.

Cystoscopic retrograde ICG, 12.5 mg diluted in 5 mL normal saline, was instilled into each ureter. White-light view at the start of surgery showed distorted adnexal anatomy with kissing ovaries, and Firefly imaging highlighted the ureteral pathway during pelvic sidewall mobilization and outlined the right ureter beneath the peritoneum during posterior dissection.

At final inspection after endometriotic disease excision and pelvic sidewall dissection, the ureters were clearly visualized with integrity and anatomical path confirmed, and fluorescence guidance confirmed ureteral preservation before closure. Retrograde ICG gave uniform and strong ureteral fluorescence, and the procedure was completed without complications.

summary.text: A 50-year-old patient with symptomatic adenomyosis, chronic pelvic pain and an endometriotic ovarian cyst was scheduled for robotic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Preoperative MRI demonstrated posterior wall adenomyosis, multiple intramural fibroids, a right ovarian endometriotic cyst, and a left hydrosalpinx. An additional finding was an ectopic left kidney without hydronephrosis, and ureteral anatomy was presumed atypical.

Intraoperative ICG near-infrared imaging at the beginning of surgery confirmed the altered ureteral course, with both ureters entering the pelvis on the right side. Fluorescence assisted entry into distorted posterior planes with dense adhesions, and at the end of the procedure verified bilateral ureteral integrity. All surgeries in the series, including this one, were completed robotically without complications.

article_limitations: The text never states the total number of patients as a number; the five cases are enumerated as Cases 1 to 5 (the title says a series of five cases), so reported_individual_count is null while the roster of five is complete.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the 11 figure images are described in the separate visual submission.
No supplementary material is listed for this article.
Case 5 ICG route and dose are not stated; the series sentence about three retrograde patients does not name them.
Discussion statements that explain fluorescence results (fibrosis restricting diffusion, urothelial uptake) are the authors' interpretation and are not recorded as patient facts.

The abstract sentence on two patients with deep infiltrating endometriosis involving the ureter does not name the cases, and its description does not match the Case 4 text (stage 3 endometriosis); its claims are not recorded as patient facts.

The introduction says three patients underwent retrograde ureteric ICG instillation for endometriosis surgery, while the case text describes retrograde instillation only for Cases 3 and 4 and gives no ICG route for Case 5.

Figure 2: the Case 2 text says Figure 2 includes a view before fluorescence activation, but the caption and the pixels show near-infrared fluorescence-mode views in both panels; no before-activation finding is recorded.
The Foley clamp durations ("five and 10 minutes, respectively") and the unlabelled dense-fibrosis sentence are kept review-only for Cases 1 and 2.
